Prospective resources should not be construed as reserves or contingent resources. Prospective resources have both an associated chance of discovery and a chance of development. Under the COGEH, a range of prospective resources estimates (low, best and high) are recommended. The following classification of prospective resources is used as presented by McDaniel: (a) Low estimate means there is at least a 90 percent probability (P90) that the quantities actually recovered will equal or exceed the low estimate; (b) Best estimate means there is at least a 50 percent probability (P50) that the quantities actually recovered will equal or exceed the median best estimate; (c) High estimate means there is at least a 10 percent probability (P10) that the quantities actually recovered will equal or exceed the high estimate; and (d) Mean estimate represents the arithmetic average of the expected recoverable volume and is the most accurate single point representation of the volume distribution. Chance of discovery, as defined in the COGEH, is the estimated probability that exploration activities will confirm the existence of a significant accumulation of potentially recoverable petroleum. Chance of development is defined as the estimated probability that, once discovered, a known accumulation will be commercially developed. Quantifying the chance of development requires consideration of both economic contingencies and other contingencies, such as legal, regulatory, market access, political, social license, internal and external approvals and commitment to project finance and development timing. As many of these factors are extremely difficult to quantify, the chance of development is uncertain and must be used with caution. The chance of commerciality is defined as the product of the chance of discovery and the chance of development. The risked mean prospective resource volumes have been determined by multiplying the unrisked mean volumes by the associated chance of commerciality. The arithmetic sum of the individual risked mean values can be considered the best estimate risked prospective resources for the portfolio as per COGEH Volume 2 Section 2.8.2. There is no certainty that any portion of the prospective resources will be discovered. If discovered, there is no certainty that it will be commercially viable to produce any portion of the prospective resources. The unrisked total is not representative of the portfolio unrisked total and is provided to give an indication of the resources range, assuming all prospects are successful. Company gross prospective resources are based on the working interest share of the property gross resources. The net present value of future net revenue of the prospective resource estimates has not been prepared and, therefore, the net prospective resources volumes are not reported. Given the uncertainty of discovery associated with the prospective resources, costs and timelines to production, as well as recovery technologies, cannot be determined at this time. For additional information regarding the Company’s prospective resources, including the significant positive and negative factors relevant to the estimate, chance of discovery and chance of development, and a description of the applicable projects and related information, see Disclosure of Contingent Resources and Prospective Resources Data – Prospective Resources: Canada. Risk Factors and Uncertainties in Estimating Quantities of Resources There are numerous uncertainties inherent in estimating quantities of resources. The resources information for the contingent and prospective resources set forth herein are estimates only. In general, estimates of resources are based upon a number of variable factors and assumptions, such as historical production from the properties, production rates, ultimate resource recovery, the timing and amount of capital expenditures, marketability of oil, NGLs and natural gas, royalty rates, the assumed effects of regulation by governmental agencies and future operating costs, all of which may vary materially from actual results. For these reasons, estimates of the resources attributable to any particular group of properties, the classification of such resources based on risk of recovery and estimates of future net revenue associated with resources prepared by different engineers, or by the same engineer at different times, may vary. Gran Tierra’s actual production, revenue, taxes and development and operating expenditures with respect to its resources will vary from estimates thereof and such variations could be material. The estimates of Gran Tierra’s resources provided herein are estimates only and there is no guarantee that the estimated resources will be recovered. Actual resources may be greater than or less than the estimates provided herein and variances could be material. With respect to the discovered resources (including contingent resources), there is uncertainty that it will be commercially viable to produce any portion of the resources. With respect to the undiscovered resources (including prospective resources), there is no certainty that any portion of the resources will be discovered. If discovered, there is no certainty that it will be commercially viable to produce any portion of the resources. There are numerous factors and uncertainties that affect the anticipated development of the Company’s resources. The chances of development for the estimated resources are subject to a number of factors, including overall project economics, the employed recovery technology or technology under development, regulatory and environmental approval, the availability of markets and production facilities and political risk to the development. The Company will be required to make substantial capital expenditures in order to prove, exploit, develop and produce oil, natural gas and NGLs from its resource properties in the future. If the Company’s cash flow from operations is not sufficient to satisfy its capital expenditure requirements, there can be no assurance that additional debt or equity financing will be available to meet these requirements or, if available, that the terms will be acceptable to the Company. Failure to obtain such financing on a timely basis could cause the Company to forfeit its interest in certain properties, miss certain opportunities, reduce its pace of development or terminate its operations on such properties. An inability of the Company to access sufficient capital for its exploration and development purposes could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s ability to execute its business strategy to develop its prospects. The significant economic factors that affect the Company’s future development of its resources are: future commodity prices for oil and natural gas (and the Company’s outlook relating to such prices); the future capital costs of drilling, completing, tying in and equipping the wells necessary to develop such lands at the relevant times; the future costs of operating wells at the relevant times; and the levels of royalties applicable to productions from such lands. The significant uncertainties that affect the Company’s development of its resources are: the ability of the Company to obtain the capital necessary to fund the development of such lands at the relevant times; the future drilling and completion results the Company achieves in its development activities (e.g. with respect to the development of particular intervals or geographic areas, the uncertainty would be whether the initial drilling and completion results are sufficient to justify the development of such interval or geographic area); drilling and completion results achieved by others on lands in proximity to the Company’s lands; transportation and processing infrastructure becoming available in a timeline consistent with proposed development plans; the availability of regulatory approvals for development of the lands and the necessary infrastructure; and governmental actions and future changes to applicable regulatory or royalty regimes that affect timing or economics of proposed development activities. Disclosures of Resources Information and Cautionary Note to U.S. Investors All estimates of contingent resources disclosed in this press release have been prepared by McDaniel in accordance with NI 51-101 and the COGEH and are derived from the GTE McDaniel Resources Report. Contingent resources are those quantities of petroleum estimated, as of a given date, to be potentially recoverable from known accumulations, but which are not currently considered to be commercially recoverable due to one or more contingencies. There is no certainty that it will be commercially viable to produce any portion of the contingent resources. Investors should not view the disclosure of contingent resources in this press release as an estimate of reserves prepared in accordance with SEC requirements. All estimates of prospective resources disclosed in this press release have been prepared by McDaniel in accordance with NI 51-101 and the COGEH and are derived from the GTE McDaniel Prospective Resources Report. Prospective resources are those quantities of petroleum estimated, as of a given date, to be potentially recoverable from undiscovered accumulations by application of future development projects and are subject to both a chance of discovery and a chance of development. There is no certainty that any portion of the prospective resources disclosed herein will be discovered or, if discovered, will be commercially viable or developed. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) permits oil and gas companies that are subject to domestic issuer reporting requirements under U.S. federal securities law, in their filings with the SEC, to disclose only estimated proved, probable and possible reserves that meet the SEC’s definitions of such terms. Investors should not view the disclosure of prospective resources in this press release as an estimate of reserves prepared in accordance with SEC requirements. Back to Press Releases

title: What Tests Do You Actually Need Postpartum? An Internist's Guide to What Should Be Checked and Why
summary: A six-week check shouldn't end with "get some rest." Learn which labs, history questions, and red flags a thorough postpartum evaluation should always include.
body_text: If your six-week postpartum visit ended with "everything looks fine, get some rest" and zero lab work, you didn't get a thorough evaluation. You got a quick check on the baby's delivery system. A real postpartum investigation covers specific labs, a careful symptom history, and a set of red flags that should never be brushed off as "just new-mom tired." I want to walk you through what I'd actually want to check, and why most of it can be done without dragging yourself and a newborn to an office. Start a chat with Dr Shirin Syed Free Describe your symptoms and get real medical guidance, on your schedule. What are we actually checking for here? This is about the diagnostic side: figuring out whether what you're feeling is normal postpartum recovery or something medical that's hiding behind it. We're not talking about treatment plans yet. We're talking about the tests and the questions that separate "exhausted because you have a newborn" from "exhausted because your ferritin is in the single digits or your thyroid just destabilized." Get this part right and the next steps become obvious. What should a thorough postpartum investigation include? History: the part that matters more than people think Delivery details. How much blood did you lose? Was there a postpartum hemorrhage, even a "minor" one? Did you need any transfusions? The answer changes whether iron-deficiency anemia is likely or almost guaranteed. Symptom trajectory. This is the most important question: is what you're feeling getting better, staying the same, or getting worse? Normal postpartum fatigue gradually improves week over week. If you're more exhausted at 10 weeks than you were at 4, that's not adaptation. That's a signal. Mood and mental health, asked directly. "Are you having thoughts that scare you?" and "Do you feel like yourself?" are two questions that change outcomes. Most new moms won't volunteer this information because they've been told what they're feeling is just part of the adjustment. A good history asks anyway. Family history. Thyroid disease in a first-degree relative raises the probability of postpartum thyroiditis. A personal or family history of depression or anxiety raises the probability of postpartum mood disorders. Medications and supplements. Are you still on a prenatal? Are you taking a standalone iron supplement? Are you breastfeeding, and has anyone adjusted your supplement regimen accordingly? Your FutureClinic doctor takes this history on the chat consultation, and the chat format actually helps here because you can think through your answers instead of trying to remember everything in a rushed 15-minute appointment while your baby is crying in the carrier. Labs: the actual panel CBC (complete blood count). Looks at hemoglobin and hematocrit, the basic screen for anemia. But a normal CBC does not rule out iron deficiency on its own, which is why the next test matters. Ferritin. This is your iron storage marker. You can have a normal hemoglobin and still be profoundly iron-depleted. Ferritin catches what the CBC misses. I want to see ferritin on every postpartum panel, especially if there was any significant bleeding. A ferritin in the single digits or teens explains fatigue that no amount of sleep will fix [per WHO iron deficiency guidelines]. TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) with Free T4. Not just TSH alone. Postpartum thyroiditis affects roughly 5–10% of women in the first year after delivery [per American Thyroid Association guidelines]. It can swing between a hyperthyroid phase (anxiety, racing heart, weight loss) and a hypothyroid phase (crushing fatigue, hair loss, brain fog, depressed mood). Every one of those symptoms gets written off as sleep deprivation unless someone checks. Free T4 tells you what the thyroid is actually doing right now, not just what the pituitary is asking it to do. Vitamin D. Deficiency is common in the general population and more common postpartum, especially in women who were deficient during pregnancy. It contributes to fatigue, mood changes, and bone health, all things that matter when you're recovering and potentially breastfeeding. Validated screening tools, done through the chat Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). This is a 10-question validated screening tool specifically designed for postpartum depression and anxiety. It takes a few minutes to complete and it catches what casual conversation misses. A score above 10 warrants a deeper conversation; a score above 13 is a strong signal for clinical depression [per ACOG Committee Opinion 757]. This can be administered through the chat consultation. You answer the questions honestly, and the doctor interprets the pattern. Prior records If you've had labs drawn at any point during pregnancy or at the six-week visit, your FutureClinic doctor can pull those through HIE (Health Information Exchange) so you're not starting from zero. Sometimes the answer is already sitting in a result from month 7 of pregnancy that nobody followed up on. What red flags change the investigation? Some symptoms are never "just adjusting." These need to be separated clearly. These are emergencies. Go to the ER or call 911, not the chat: Chest pain or severe shortness of breath at rest or with minimal activity. That's postpartum cardiomyopathy until proven otherwise. It can present weeks to months after delivery. Severe headache that won't resolve, especially with visual changes or elevated blood pressure. Postpartum preeclampsia can happen weeks after delivery. Most people don't realize that. Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby. This is an emergency, full stop, and there is no shame in it. Call 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline), go to your nearest ER, or call 911. Heavy bleeding that soaks through a pad in an hour or less. High fever with chills, which could signal postpartum endometritis or another infection. Sudden severe leg swelling or pain on one side. Postpartum blood clot risk is real and elevated for weeks after delivery. None of these are "just adjusting." Do not start a chat for these. Get emergency care. These are red flags that warrant prompt evaluation, and the chat consultation is the right place to start: Fatigue that's getting worse, not better, past 6–8 weeks. Normal trajectory is gradual improvement. Worsening fatigue is a lab signal. Heart racing at rest without an obvious trigger. Could be thyroid. Could be anemia. Could be anxiety. All checkable. Hair loss that feels disproportionate or isn't slowing down by 6 months postpartum. Telogen effluvium is real and usually self-resolving, but hair loss can also be a sign of iron deficiency or thyroid dysfunction. If you just write it off as "hormonal," you might miss something treatable that's making it worse or making it last longer. Persistent anxiety that's interfering with bonding or daily function. Checking the baby's breathing every 10 minutes, unable to put the baby down, intrusive thoughts that won't stop. That's not "normal new-mom worry." That's a condition, and it responds to treatment. Persistent swelling, especially in the legs or face, beyond the first few weeks. Each of these pairs with a concrete next step your doctor would take on the chat: ordering the right labs, screening for mood disorders, or having the conversation about whether something more needs to happen. What should you do first, and what can you keep monitoring? First priority: If you had any significant bleeding during or after delivery, get a CBC and ferritin checked. Iron-deficiency anemia is the most common and most fixable thing hiding behind postpartum exhaustion, and it won't get better on its own without repletion. Same priority: If your mood is consistently low, numb, or anxious in a way that feels bigger than situational stress, or if you're having intrusive thoughts, bring it up now. Not next month. Now. The EPDS screening takes minutes and opens the door to treatment that works. Within the first few months: Get a thyroid panel (TSH + Free T4). Postpartum thyroiditis can present anywhere from 1 to 12 months after delivery. If you're at 8 weeks and your energy is tanking while your heart races for no reason, this is worth checking sooner rather than later. Ongoing monitoring: Track your mood. Even if it's just one word a day in a notes app on your phone. Two weeks of "terrible" or "numb" is data you bring to your doctor. Track your energy trajectory: is it improving, flat, or declining? That trajectory is the most useful piece of information for distinguishing normal recovery from something medical. Start a chat with Dr Shirin Syed Free Describe your symptoms and get real medical guidance, on your schedule. What are the most common postpartum investigation mistakes I see? 1. Checking TSH alone and calling it a complete thyroid screen. TSH is a screening test. It tells you what the pituitary is asking the thyroid to do. It doesn't tell you what the thyroid is actually producing right now. In postpartum thyroiditis, the TSH can lag behind what's actually happening. Free T4 fills that gap. Skipping it is the most common shortcut I see, and it misses the women who are actively symptomatic from thyroid dysfunction even when the TSH hasn't caught up yet. 2. Skipping ferritin because the CBC came back normal. This one genuinely frustrates me. A woman can have a hemoglobin of 12, technically "normal," and a ferritin of 8. She's profoundly iron-depleted. Her body is running on fumes. And because the CBC looked fine on paper, nobody dug deeper. Ferritin should be on every postpartum panel. I personally include it even when the hemoglobin is normal. Other doctors may not, and that's a legitimate difference in practice style. But I've seen too many women suffer for months with something a simple lab would have caught. 3. Treating the six-week visit as the finish line. The system gives new moms one postpartum visit and then essentially says "good luck." But postpartum thyroiditis can present at 3 months. Postpartum depression can present at 6 months. The body is still in upheaval well beyond week six. One visit is a starting point, not a conclusion. 4. Attributing every symptom to sleep deprivation without checking. Yes, you're sleep-deprived. Of course you are. But sleep deprivation doesn't cause your ferritin to drop to single digits. Sleep deprivation doesn't destabilize your thyroid. The overlap between "tired new mom" and "anemic or hypothyroid new mom" is almost perfect on symptoms alone. You can only separate them by running the labs. It's better to check and have everything come back normal than to assume and miss something that was treatable the whole time. 5. Not asking about mood directly. If you wait for a new mom to volunteer that she's having intrusive thoughts or that she doesn't feel bonded to her baby, you'll be waiting a long time. She's been conditioned to believe that struggling means failing. The questions have to be asked directly, without judgment, every time. "Are you having thoughts that scare you?" is a question that changes outcomes. When is in-person care genuinely needed? For most postpartum symptoms, your FutureClinic doctor can take a detailed history through the chat, order the right labs, screen for postpartum depression, pull your prior records, and start treatment for the most likely cause based on what we find. How you respond confirms we're on the right track or tells us to pivot. The same doctor stays with you through the follow-up. You message when something changes, when a side effect comes up, when you need a dose adjusted. No rebooking. No being passed to someone new. If we still can't get to the bottom of it through the chat consultation and any initial treatment trial, or if your symptoms suggest something like postpartum cardiomyopathy that needs cardiac imaging or an in-person cardiac evaluation, your FutureClinic doctor can talk through whether that's actually needed for your case. In most situations we can get you to a clear answer and a working treatment plan from home first. We only recommend in-person when there's an absolute need for it, and the goal is always to get you treated quickly, safely, and effectively from home whenever possible. Frequently asked questions What blood tests should I ask for after having a baby? At minimum: a CBC, ferritin, TSH with Free T4, and vitamin D. If you had significant bleeding during or after delivery, iron studies become even more important. If you have symptoms of a mood disorder, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale is a validated screening tool your doctor can walk you through. These aren't exotic tests. They're basic labs that catch the most common conditions hiding behind "normal new-mom tired." How do I know if my fatigue is normal postpartum exhaustion or something medical? Trajectory. Normal postpartum fatigue gradually improves as you and the baby settle into a rhythm (even if slowly). If your fatigue is flat or getting worse at 6, 8, 10 weeks, or if it feels disproportionate to your sleep situation, that's a signal to check labs. You can't tell the difference by how it feels. You can only tell by checking. Can postpartum thyroid problems really cause all of these symptoms? Yes. Postpartum thyroiditis can cause fatigue, hair loss, heart palpitations, mood changes, weight changes, brain fog, and anxiety. It affects roughly 5–10% of women in the first year after delivery. Every one of those symptoms gets attributed to sleep deprivation and stress unless someone checks a thyroid panel. Is it normal that I don't feel bonded to my baby? It can be. Bonding isn't always instant, and it doesn't always look like the movies. But if the lack of bonding is accompanied by persistent sadness, numbness, or intrusive thoughts, it might be postpartum depression, and that is treatable. You are not a bad mom for feeling that way. You might just need help, and that's okay. Do I really need to go in for an appointment, or can this be done through chat? The history, the lab orders, the mood screening, the follow-up: all of that can be done through a chat consultation. You don't need to find childcare, drive to an office, and sit in a waiting room with a newborn to get these answers. Your doctor reviews your history, orders the labs, interprets the results, and starts treatment if needed, all through the chat, on your schedule. If something comes back that genuinely needs in-person evaluation, your doctor will tell you and help you figure out the next step. When should I worry about postpartum hair loss? Some hair shedding after delivery is expected. Telogen effluvium is a real physiological process triggered by the hormonal shift, and it usually resolves on its own by 6–12 months. But if the shedding feels severe, isn't slowing down, or is accompanied by fatigue or other symptoms, it's worth checking ferritin and thyroid function. Iron deficiency and thyroid dysfunction can both worsen or prolong hair loss that would otherwise have resolved. How long after delivery can postpartum depression or anxiety show up? It can present anytime in the first year, though it most commonly shows up in the first 3–6 months. Postpartum anxiety specifically, the kind with intrusive thoughts, hypervigilance, and an inability to relax even when the baby is safe, often gets missed because it doesn't look like the "classic" image of postpartum depression. Both respond to treatment. Both are worth screening for. Now you can either keep trying to figure this out yourself with online resources, or you can start a chat consultation with a real doctor who can take your full history, order the right labs, screen for postpartum depression, and actually stay with you through the follow-up, usually with a response back the same day. No booking, no video calls, no waiting weeks. You start it from your phone whenever you're ready. For one-to-one guidance on your specific situation, talk to your own doctor — or start a chat consultation with a FutureClinic doctor and get a real, personalized answer for your case. title: Investor panel: What it takes to build a fundable biotech – with Life Science Nation
summary: Learn what makes an early-stage biotech investable, from development strategy to exit planning. Free webinar with Certara and Life Science Nation.
body_text: Share Share Share Date: Thursday, August 20, 2026 Time: 9:00 AM – 4:30 PM Early Clinical Regulatory Strategic Leadership Services: Drug Development Support Register Most biotech companies don’t fail to raise capital because the science is wrong. They fail because investors can’t see a credible path from discovery to value creation. In partnership with Life Science Nation, this webinar brings together investors, founders, and drug development strategists to unpack what actually makes an early-stage biotech investable beyond biology. The panel will cover how to align science, team, and capital strategy; why exit planning needs to start on day one; and the specific credibility gaps that make investors walk away. Key learning objectives: What investors are really evaluating when they assess an early-stage asset and the difference between compelling biology and development readiness How to build the “Tripod” of science, people, and capital so they mature together instead of working against each other Why identifying your likely acquirer or partner early increases optionality and strengthens your pitch The green flags and red flags investors look for in a development plan, and the credibility gaps that undermine even strong science How to think beyond your next financing round anticipating shifts in regulatory environments, standard of care, and capital markets This webinar is ideal for Pre-Series A to Series B biotech founders CSOs and CEOs Translational medicine leaders Business development leaders Investors evaluating early-stage assets Speakers: Fran Brown, PhD Senior Vice President, Global Head, Drug Development Science Fran has over 25 years of experience with strategic and operational global drug development from early discovery to filing and post-marketing. She possesses a broad knowledge of strategic drug discovery and development, with a special focus on development strategy and the application of model-informed drug development (MIDD). Allen Hakimi Managing Director, Technomark Life Sciences Allen Hakimi, Managing Director and CEO of Technomark. Mr. Hakimi joined Technomark Consulting Service Ltd. in the UK in 2006 and has successfully led its corporate transition to Technomark Life Sciences, which now invests via a co-development business model, by sharing the cost of pre-clinical development in exchange for downstream remuneration. Under this new co-funding model, Technomark has invested in 14 development programs, with successful exits of three programs through large pharma (Wyeth/Pfizer, BMS, D-Pharm Israel), and a fourth through IPO. Jayanth Batchu Senior Associate / EIR, Xontogeny Jayanth is a Senior Associate at Xontogeny leveraging his diverse skill set to aid the due diligence efforts of the Xontogeny investment team. Jayanth is experienced in building up multiple biotech and medtech ideas including cell therapies (cancer & autoimmune), engineered enzymes & antibodies, core needle biopsy devices, infectious disease diagnostics, and urinary microvalves. Over the course of advancing prior projects, Jay has been involved with TuckLab and Tuck-Magnuson Startup Incubator and is driven to aid in the advancement of biomedical innovations. Jayanth received an AB degree in Economics from Dartmouth College, a BE degree in Biomedical Engineering and MEng degree in Biological/Chemical Engineering from Dartmouth’s Thayer School of Engineering. While at Dartmouth, Jay was an active member of the Dartmouth Entrepreneurial Network (DEN) Associates/Magnuson Center Student Leadership Board. body_text: When disaster strikes, families often face impossible decisions. For many pet owners, one of the hardest choices is whether to stay with their beloved animals or seek shelter without them. Following a powerful earthquake in southern Japan, one veterinary hospital stepped up to ensure no family had to make that heartbreaking sacrifice. An animal hospital in Kumamoto has transformed part of its facility into an emergency shelter where evacuees can stay alongside their pets. The initiative has offered comfort and security to dozens of people who were forced to flee their homes after the earthquake caused widespread destruction. Earthquake Leaves Communities Displaced A strong earthquake shook southern Japan, damaging homes and disrupting essential services across affected areas. Thousands of residents were left without electricity and running water, while emergency teams continued rescue and recovery operations. The disaster has claimed at least 36 lives, according to reports, and many communities are still working to restore normal services. Families who evacuated their homes faced uncertain conditions as temporary shelters filled with residents seeking safety. While emergency accommodation was available for many people, pet owners encountered a familiar challenge. Numerous evacuation centers either restrict animals or do not allow them inside shared living spaces due to concerns about allergies, hygiene, noise, and the comfort of other evacuees. A Difficult Choice for Pet Owners For 31 year old factory worker Tomoko Takaoka, the earthquake quickly became more than a struggle for shelter. She was unable to contact her parents after the quake and urgently needed a safe place to stay. She gathered her two beloved dogs, Ku, a Chihuahua, and Sheri, a Chihuahua Poodle mix, and headed to a nearby evacuation center. However, she soon discovered that her pets were not welcome. Rather than leave her dogs behind, Takaoka chose to remain with them. The trio spent the first night inside her vehicle despite the uncomfortable summer heat. For many pet owners, animals are not simply companions. They are members of the family. Leaving them behind during a crisis is often emotionally impossible. Social Media Leads to a Lifeline Hope arrived through social media. After reading online posts, Takaoka learned that Ryunosuke Animal Hospital in Kumamoto had opened its doors to both people and their pets. The veterinary hospital quickly converted classrooms from its veterinary nursing school into temporary accommodation for evacuees. Separate rooms were prepared for dog owners and cat owners to create a more comfortable environment for both animals and people. This thoughtful arrangement helped reduce stress while allowing families to remain together throughout the emergency. Lessons Learned From the 2016 Kumamoto Earthquake The hospital's decision was not made overnight. It was shaped by experience. Following the devastating Kumamoto earthquake in 2016, staff members recognized a major gap in disaster preparedness involving pets. Many owners struggled to find accommodation where animals were accepted, creating unnecessary hardship during an already traumatic time. Hospital director Ryunosuke Tokuda explained that keeping pets with their owners benefits both people and animals during emergencies. He also acknowledged the reality that not everyone is comfortable sharing space with pets. Concerns about allergies, odors, fleas, and noise can create challenges inside crowded evacuation centers. By creating designated areas specifically for pet owners, the hospital found a practical solution that respects the needs of everyone involved. Emergency Shelter Opens Once Again Following the latest earthquake, the hospital immediately reopened its emergency shelter. When journalists visited the facility, 26 evacuees and their pets were staying there. Inside tents and temporary living spaces, owners were able to care for their animals while also receiving shelter themselves. For Takaoka, being able to remain with Ku and Sheri brought significant emotional relief. She explained that her dogs occasionally become excited when meeting other animals in the designated dog area, but she is able to calm them quickly. Although she hopes to return home soon, her greatest comfort comes from knowing that her pets remain by her side. She described them simply as family and said she wants to stay with them whenever possible. Why Pet Friendly Disaster Shelters Matter Natural disasters often highlight overlooked issues within emergency planning. Many evacuation centers focus on meeting basic human needs such as food, water, and medical care. While these priorities are essential, pets are also an important part of countless households. Research has shown that some people delay evacuation or refuse to leave dangerous areas if they cannot bring their animals with them. This can place both people and rescue workers at greater risk. Pet friendly shelters help eliminate this difficult choice by providing safe accommodation for entire families. Facilities like Ryunosuke Animal Hospital demonstrate that thoughtful planning can create practical solutions without compromising the comfort of other evacuees. A Model That Could Inspire Others As climate related disasters, earthquakes, floods, and severe weather events continue to affect communities worldwide, the need for inclusive emergency planning becomes increasingly important. The Kumamoto hospital offers an example that other communities could consider when preparing for future emergencies. Designating separate areas for pets, ensuring veterinary support is available, and planning accommodations in advance can significantly improve disaster response for both people and animals. These measures not only protect pets but also provide emotional stability for owners who may already be coping with tremendous stress and uncertainty. Compassion During Crisis The earthquake has left many families facing difficult days ahead as recovery efforts continue across southern Japan. Despite the destruction, stories like this highlight the compassion and creativity shown by local organizations during times of crisis. By opening its classrooms and welcoming animals alongside their owners, Ryunosuke Animal Hospital has provided more than temporary housing. It has offered reassurance that families do not have to face disaster alone or leave behind those they love most. For many evacuees, staying together with their pets has made an incredibly difficult situation just a little more bearable. Source: The Independent . title: Canton Strategic Holdings, Inc. Releases Second Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Results
summary: Records first operating revenue from locking service and Super Validator operations
body_text: Records first operating revenue from locking service and Super Validator operations Completes sale of legacy biotechnology subsidiary Gravitas NEW YORK, Aug. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Canton Strategic Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: CNTN ) ("Canton Strategic" or the "Company"), the first publicly traded company to leverage Canton Coin ("CC") to support the Canton Network's ability to digitize traditional financial markets, today released financial and operating results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. "We are pleased to see our disciplined strategy and operational focus pay off with meaningful operating revenue recognized in the second quarter," said Mark Wendland, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Canton Strategic Holdings. "Since launching our strategy in November 2025, we have taken a diversified approach to value accretion, seeking opportunities to capitalize on commercial ventures that align with our long-term conviction in the Canton Network's ability to transform financial markets." During the quarter, the Company recorded its first operating revenue, reflecting the initial contribution from its Super Validator operations and its locking-as-a-service ("LaaS") offering on the Canton Network, establishing the Company's base of revenue generating business operations. Notably, its LaaS offering drove revenue of approximately $1.3 million (see "Other Revenue" in financial tables below). This offering, launched in April 2026, supports Super Validators and Featured Applications who are required under Canton Improvement Proposals ("CIP") 0105 and CIP-0116 to maintain locked CC balances. Through this service, the Company locks its own CC on a customer's behalf while retaining legal and beneficial ownership, and is compensated through a stated interest rate, a share of the customer's network rewards, or an equity grant earned over the contract term, depending on the arrangement. Separately, the Company's Validator and Super Validator operations drove $191,226 in revenue during this quarter, representing CC rewards earned for providing validation and liveness services to the network. "Our Super Validator and locking-as-a-service operations reflect the active role we intend to play as the network scales, supporting the builders and validators driving institutional adoption of blockchain infrastructure," continued Wendland. "Our growing operating business, alongside our Canton Coin treasury, gives shareholders a differentiated way to gain exposure to the network's adoption, rather than passive exposure to a single token." Quarterly Highlights (as of June 30, 2026) Secured approval for an expanded Super Validator weight of 15 under CIP-0102 and CIP-0114. Active minting at 0.5 weight began in May 2026, with the remaining 14.5 weight scheduled to unlock in tranches through the first quarter of 2028 as the Company meets specific deliverables and receives approval from the Canton Foundation's Accountability Committee. Importantly, a higher weight indicates a proportionally larger claim on the CC minted to Super Validators. Launched its first commercial offering, locking-as-a-service ("LaaS"), to Canton Network Super Validators and Featured Applications. This model compensates the Company via a daily interest rate on locked CC, a share of network rewards, or an equity grant earned over a one-year term. Recognized revenue through diversified income streams, including $1,304,633 largely from its LaaS program, as well as $191,226 from its Network validation activities, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, the Company's first quarter generating revenue under its digital asset treasury strategy. Streamlined its operations through the sale of Gravitas Life Sciences, Inc. ("Gravitas"), the Company's legacy clinical-stage biotechnology subsidiary, on July 17, 2026, in exchange for an unsecured promissory note in the original principal amount of $3,500,000 bearing 15% payment-in-kind interest, plus contingent development milestone payments. Strengthened its governance through the election of Sean Galvin, Pamela L. Carter, and Rishi Nangalia as directors at the Company's 2026 annual meeting on July 13, 2026. Mr. Galvin, Ms. Carter, and Mr. Nangalia collectively bring deep experience across financial markets, public company oversight, and technology to the Company's Board. Created optionality for opportunistic share repurchases through Board approval of a $50 million share repurchase program on June 11, 2026; no shares were repurchased under the program during the period. Canton Coin holdings of 3,714,204,876 units with a fair value of $523,353,752, up from $501,760,369 as of December 31, 2025 Cost basis of CC holdings of $584,064,579 as of June 30, 2026, compared to $523,770,731 as of December 31, 2025 Cash and cash equivalents of $37,241,568 as of June 30, 2026, up from $12,007,148 as of December 31, 2025. Financial Highlights (Three Months Ended June 30, 2026) Total revenue of $1,495,859 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $0 for the same period in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA of ($820,449) for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to ($1,126,984) for the same period in 2025. Adjusted Operating Expenses of $2,628,156, compared to $1,122,991 in the same period in 2025. Adjusted Operating Expenses Coverage Ratio of 56.9%, compared to 0.0% in the same period in 2025, reflecting the first recognized revenue in the current period. Net loss of $19,254,826, or $(0.08) per basic and diluted share from continuing operations, for the three months ended June 30, 2026. Unrealized loss on digital asset holdings of $23,735,950 for the three months ended June 30, 2026, reflecting a decline in the reference price of CC relative to the Company's weighted-average cost basis; the Company held no digital assets prior to November 2025. Total assets of $564,570,386 and total stockholders' equity of $454,902,612 as of June 30, 2026, compared to total assets of $519,146,435 and total stockholders' equity of $397,925,880 at December 31, 2025. Business Update Super Validator Operations The Company operates as a Super Validator ("SV") on the Canton Network. SVs earn Canton Coin based on their approved "weight," which functions like a share count: a higher weight means a proportionally larger claim on the CC minted to Super Validators in each network round. Weight unlocks in tranches as the Company meets specific deliverables and receives approval from the Canton Foundation's Accountability Committee. Each unlock triggers ongoing per-round minting plus a one-time catch-up mint of rewards that had accumulated in escrow while that weight awaited approval. Active minting began on May 9, 2026, when the Company met the first of eight deliverables under CIP-0102. For the period from that date through June 30, 2026, the Company recognized Network validation revenue of $191,226 on its active 0.5 weight, its first revenue from Super Validator operations, which included a one-time catch-up mint of rewards accumulated in escrow since January 21, 2026, when CIP-0102 was approved. As of June 30, 2026, the Company held total approved SV weight of 15 (4 under CIP-0102, 11 under CIP-0114) and an active weight of 0.5. The remaining 14.5 is expected to unlock through the first quarter of 2028 as follows: If achieved on schedule, active weight would grow thirty-fold, from 0.5 to the full 15, by the first quarter of 2028. Under CIP-0114, the Company's allocated SV weight is subject to quarterly review and a continuing requirement that the Company maintain CC holdings at or above the applicable CC Quantum established under the program. Assuming that requirement continues to be satisfied, 50% of the applicable allocated weight becomes eligible for release following the first quarterly review, and one-fourth of the remaining 50% becomes eligible for release at each of the next four quarterly reviews. Locking-as-a-Service Canton Network rules (CIP-0105 for Super Validators, CIP-0116 for Featured Applications) require those participants to keep a minimum amount of CC locked to maintain their status and reward eligibility. Through its LaaS offering, the Company locks its own CC on a customer's behalf so the customer can satisfy that requirement without sourcing CC itself. The Company retains full ownership of the CC throughout; only a wallet identifier, not custody or title, is shared with the Canton Foundation for compliance verification. LaaS launched on April 23, 2026. Non -GAAP Measures of Financial Performance In addition to financial measures presented under generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America ("GAAP"), the Company evaluates performance using non-GAAP financial measures including adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ("Adjusted EBITDA") and Adjusted Operating Expenses, and Adjusted Operating Expenses Coverage Ratio. Adjusted EBITDA The Company defines Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss), excluding income tax provision (benefit), stock-based compensation expense, unrealized gains or losses on digital asset holdings, and other non-recurring items. Management believes this financial measure provides a performance measurement that reflects our recurring core business operations. Adjusted EBITDA is provided in addition to, and should not be considered a substitute for, GAAP financial measures. Adjusted EBITDA has limitations as a financial measure, should be considered as supplemental in nature, and is not meant as a substitute for the related financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Adjusted Operating Expenses Adjusted Operating Expenses is defined as GAAP total operating expenses minus stock-based compensation expense, which the Company believes is not indicative of its ongoing expenses. The amount and timing of the excluded items are unpredictable, are not driven by core results of operations, and render comparisons with prior periods less meaningful. Adjusted Operating Expenses Coverage Ratio Adjusted Operating Expenses Coverage Ratio is calculated as Adjusted Operating Expenses divided by total revenues. The following table reconciles Adjusted EBITDA to net loss, its most directly comparable GAAP measure for the periods indicated. It also reconciles Adjusted Operating Expenses to operating expenses, its most directly comparable GAAP measure for the periods indicated. About Canton Strategic Holdings, Inc. Canton Strategic Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: CNTN ), is the first publicly traded company to leverage Canton Coin and support the Canton Network to advance institutional blockchain adoption and the digitization of financial markets. In addition to its operating business that drives value through activities on the Canton Network, the Company is a strategic investor in the Canton ecosystem. title: Array Labs Expands Strategic Partnerships to Accelerate Global 3D Mapping
summary: Array Labs is working to provide high-quality 3D imagery on a global scale.
body_text: PALO ALTO, CA, February 26, 2025 – Array Labs, developer of the world's first 3D-imaging satellite constellation, today announced several strategic relationships to accelerate deployment of its breakthrough technology platform. John Deere (NYSE: DE) recently announced that it has selected Array Labs for its prestigious 2025 Startup Collaborator program to explore applications of high-resolution 3D mapping in the ag and heavy industry markets. Additionally, Array Labs announced today that it has received an investment from In-Q-Tel (IQT), the strategic investor that identifies innovative technologies to support the U.S. national security community and America’s allies. As part of the investment, IQT Managing Partner Tom Gillespie will join Array Labs' board as an observer. These new relationships build on Array's collaboration with Umbra and Raytheon (NYSE: RTX), announced in January 2025, which is accelerating the development of Site3D, Array's first commercial product combining state-of-the-art radar with advanced algorithms to create detailed 3D models of Earth's surface. Array Labs is also proud to be enrolled in NVIDIA’s Inception program and the exclusive Esri Startup Program , which will help expand access to Array's 3D data products across Esri's extensive network of geospatial technology users worldwide. Transforming How We See and Understand Our Planet Array's distributed satellite architecture combines formation flight technologies and advanced radar systems to collect detailed global data through any weather conditions, day or night. The company's space systems and processing pipeline deliver native 3D data, with sub-meter resolution and frequent global updates – achievements previously impossible with conventional satellites. These capabilities mark a fundamental shift in how governments, Fortune 500 companies, and civil organizations monitor and understand our changing planet, enabling: "This momentum reflects growing recognition of our technology's transformative potential," said Andrew Peterson, CEO and cofounder of Array Labs. "Working with leaders across agriculture, defense, and geospatial, among other sectors, significantly expands our ability to deliver breakthrough capabilities to our customers worldwide." These announcements come at a pivotal time for Array Labs, following the successful 2024 launch of two demonstration satellites, multiple contract wins with the U.S. Department of Defense, and growing commercial interest in the forthcoming Site3D product line.

title: Core Scientific Completes Acquisition of Polaris DS, Advancing Planned Muskogee Expansion to 1.5 GW of Gross Power

body_text: Core Scientific Completes Acquisition of Polaris DS, Advancing Planned Muskogee Expansion to 1.5 GW of Gross Power August 14, 2026 7:00 am EDT Download as PDF MIAMI--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Core Scientific, Inc. (Nasdaq: CORZ) (“Core Scientific” or the “Company”), a leader in digital infrastructure for high-density colocation (“HDC”), today announced that it has completed its previously announced acquisition of Polaris DS LLC (“Polaris”). Through the acquisition, Core Scientific has secured the approximately 440 currently in service megawatts (“MW”) of gross, grid-connected power capacity being used by Polaris under existing electric service agreements with Oklahoma Gas & Electric. The aggregate purchase price for the acquisition was approximately $444 million in cash. “The Polaris acquisition is another example of how we are strategically expanding our power portfolio to support our long-term growth,” said Adam Sullivan, Chief Executive Officer of Core Scientific. “Through site acquisitions this year, we have added more than 600 MW of leasable power to our portfolio, while continuing to further scale our campuses.” Core Scientific reiterates its plan to scale its Muskogee campus to approximately 1.5 GW of gross power, or approximately 1.0 GW of leasable power, through a combination of grid-connected and behind-the-meter solutions. The Company is on track to deliver the next approximately 82 MW at Muskogee to its customer beginning in the second half of 2027. About Core Scientific, Inc. Core Scientific is a leader in designing, building and operating large scale, purpose-built data centers for high-density colocation (“HDC”) services. Core Scientific operates facilities for high-density colocation services serving artificial intelligence-related (“AI”) workloads and is a premier provider of digital infrastructure and services to its third-party customers. The majority of the Company's revenue is derived from high-density colocation services, with the remainder derived from earning digital assets for the Company's own account and from digital asset mining hosting services. The Company is in the process of repurposing its remaining mining facilities to support its high-density colocation services business as circumstances allow. Core Scientific’s facilities are located in Alabama (1), Georgia (2), Kentucky (1), North Carolina (1), North Dakota (1), Oklahoma (1) and Texas (4). To learn more, visit www.corescientific.com . title: CLEAR Airport Guide: Boston Logan International Airport
summary: Flying through Boston Logan International Airport? Discover where to eat, shop, and relax, and the best ways to plan ahead with airport tips & recommendations from CLEAR.
body_text: Boston Logan International Airport (BOS), commonly known as Boston Logan, is New England's largest airport and the primary hub serving Boston and the surrounding region. From local dining and New England-inspired shopping to exhibits celebrating the region's history, here's everything you need to turn your travel day into a great day at Boston Logan. ‍ Why Fly Through Boston Logan? Boston connects travelers to destinations across North America, Europe, Latin America, and beyond, while offering one of the country's most convenient airport locations. Just a few miles from downtown Boston, it's easy to reach whether you're visiting the city or connecting to other parts of the world. The airport's four terminals serve a mix of domestic and international airlines, offering many nonstop destinations while remaining easy to navigate compared to many major U.S. airports. ‍ Did You Know? Much of Boston Logan sits on land reclaimed from Boston Harbor. Since opening in 1923, the airport has expanded well beyond its original footprint to become New England's busiest airport. ‍ Experience the Best of New England at Boston Logan Boston Logan is more than a place to catch a flight—it's an introduction to New England. From fresh seafood and local breweries to exhibits celebrating the region's history and culture, the airport offers a glimpse of what makes New England unique. Where to Eat at Boston Logan Boston's food scene is built on fresh seafood, neighborhood institutions, and local breweries. You can experience all three and more before your flight. Our CLEAR Ambassadors share their favorite local spots below. You'll find Legal Sea Foods in Terminals A, B, C, and E, making it easy to enjoy New England seafood no matter where you're flying from. Order a bowl of their award-winning clam chowder or a classic lobster roll before you take off. In Terminal A, pair a local craft beer at Harpoon Tap Room with a classic lobster roll from Roger Fish Co. If you're departing from Terminal B, stop by Cisco Brewers or Kelly's Roast Beef, one of the Boston area's most iconic sandwich shops. Travelers in Terminal C can choose between Davio's Northern Italian Steakhouse for an upscale meal or Santarpio's Pizza, one of East Boston's best-known pizzerias. Before an international flight from Terminal E, enjoy locally inspired cocktails at Boston Harbor Distillery or visit Monica's Mercato, an outpost of the beloved North End specialty market. No trip to Boston feels complete without Dunkin'. With locations before and after airport security in every terminal, it's an easy stop for coffee, breakfast, or a donut before your flight. Where to Shop at Boston Logan Looking for a last-minute gift or souvenir? Browse New England Collections in Terminal A for regional keepsakes, shop Vineyard Vines in Terminal B for classic New England style, or stop by The Black Dog in Terminal C for apparel and gifts inspired by Martha's Vineyard. ‍ Make the Most of Your Time at Boston Logan Whether you have extra time before boarding or several hours between flights, Boston Logan offers plenty to explore. Before You Board Boston Logan features stores and exhibits that celebrate New England's history, culture, sports, and aviation. Sports fans can explore exhibits that showcase Boston's legendary teams and athletes in Terminal B, while the Tuskegee Airmen exhibit in Terminal C honors the first Black military aviators in the U.S. Army Air Corps, whose service helped shape aviation history. In Terminal E, discover the Hall of Flags, where more than 50 flags represent countries with nonstop service to and from Boston, and Logan 100, an exhibit celebrating the airport's first century and its role in connecting New England to the world. If you have extra time before boarding, Terminal E offers sweeping views of Boston Harbor, the downtown skyline, and arriving aircraft. ‍ Did You Know? American flags fly outside Gate B32 in Terminal B and Gate C19 in Terminal C, marking the departure gates of American Airlines Flight 11 and United Airlines Flight 175 on September 11, 2001. The flags serve as a lasting tribute to the passengers and crews who lost their lives that day. Extra Time at Boston Logan If you have an hour or more before boarding, consider exploring another terminal to discover additional New England restaurants, regional retailers, and airport exhibits. The free Massport shuttle makes it easy to travel between terminals before airport security, while Terminals A and B are connected by pedestrian walkways. What to Do During a Long Layover Boston Logan is just a few miles from downtown Boston, making it one of the easiest major airports for exploring the city during a layover. If you have several hours to spare, the MBTA Silver Line SL1 provides free service from the airport to South Station, where you can connect to many of Boston's most popular neighborhoods and attractions. Just be sure to allow enough time to return, get through airport security, and reach your gate. Tips for Tight Connection If you're connecting to another flight, check your departure gate after landing. Your next flight may depart from a different terminal. While some terminals are connected by pedestrian walkways, others require the free Massport shuttle. ‍ Enjoy a Seamless Travel Day at Boston Logan Whether you're traveling with family or need a hand navigating the airport, Boston Logan offers services to help make for an experience. Plan Ahead with Helpful Apps Before heading to the airport, download the free CLEAR App to take control of your travel day from home to gate. With the free CLEAR App, know exactly when to leave based on current traffic, real-time airport conditions, live security wait times, and the walk to your gate. Enjoy a Stress-Free Travel Day with CLEAR Concierge CLEAR Concierge is your personal airport concierge for a stress-free airport experience. Your dedicated CLEAR Ambassador meets you at the curb when you arrive, helps with bags and check-in, and brings you straight through airport security and to your gate or lounge. If you're arriving at Boston Logan, CLEAR Concierge Arrival Service greets you at the gate when you land, helps with your bags, and brings you straight to ground transportation or your connecting flight. Accessibility at Boston Logan Boston Logan offers wheelchair assistance, family restrooms, nursing rooms, service animal relief areas, and additional accessibility services throughout the airport. Visit the airport’s official accessibility page for the latest information, and contact your airline before you travel if you need accessibility assistance. ‍ Hidden Disabilities Sunflower Boston Logan is a proud member of the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower program. Travelers with non-visible disabilities, including autism, dementia, anxiety, or chronic pain, can request a Sunflower lanyard as a discreet way to let airport staff know they may benefit from additional support, assistance, or simply a little more time during their journey. For more information or to request a lanyard, visit an airport information booth to connect with Customer Service through the Virtual Assistant or call 1-800-23-LOGAN. ‍ Sensory and Accessibility Support Travelers with sensory sensitivities can use the airport's Sensory/Calming Room in Terminal E, located post-security near Gate E15. The space includes calming, tactile features and an airplane simulation room to help passengers prepare for the travel experience. Boston Logan also partners with Aira , a free visual interpreting service that connects travelers who are blind or have low vision with trained live agents through a mobile app or assistive smart glasses. Agents can provide step-by-step guidance from the curb through check-in, airport security, and all the way to your gate. Travelers who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have difficulty speaking can access relay services through the Voice Massachusetts Relay System, and TTY assistance is also available through the Boston Logan Call Center. ‍ BOS PAWS Need a moment to relax before your flight? BOS PAWS , Boston Logan's therapy dog program in partnership with Alliance of Therapy Dogs, brings certified therapy dogs into the terminals to help reduce travel stress. You might meet Belle the Great Pyrenees, Campbell the Labrador Retriever, Remi the Giant Schnauzer, Waffles the French Bulldog, or one of the other friendly members of the BOS PAWS crew. ‍ Navigating Boston Logan Know Your Terminal Boston Logan has four terminals: A, B, C, and E. Terminal A primarily serves Delta Air Lines, Terminal B serves American Airlines, United Airlines, Southwest Airlines, and Air Canada, Terminal C is home to JetBlue and several regional carriers, while Terminal E handles most international arrivals and departures. Gate assignments occasionally change, so check Boston Logan's official airline directory before your trip to confirm your departure terminal. Moving Between Terminals The free Massport shuttle connects all four terminals, the Rental Car Center, Airport Station on the MBTA Blue Line, and the airport's water transportation dock. Terminals A and B are connected by pedestrian walkways before airport security. Other terminal transfers require the Massport shuttle. If you leave the secure area to change terminals, you'll need to clear airport security again before heading to your gate. Airport Security Each terminal has its own airport security checkpoint, and wait times vary throughout the day. CLEAR+ Lanes are available in Terminals A, B, C, and E. ‍ Not a CLEAR+ Member? Join today to unlock exclusive access to over 150 CLEAR+ Lanes across 62 airports nationwide, so you can speed through airport security in seconds.

title: Self-Insuring vs. Basic Coverage: Weighing the Risks for Florida Homeowners
body_text: Thinking about skipping home insurance to save money? It might not be worth the risk - especially in Florida. While sunny skies and palm trees are part of everyday life, so are hurricanes and rising insurance premiums. Homeowners face a tough choice: go without insurance, opt for minimal coverage, or find a solution that balances cost and protection. In this blog, we break down the real financial risks of self-insuring in Florida and introduce how dwelling fire insurance, like ValueGuard Property Insurance ®, can offer affordable, essential coverage. Why Self-Insuring Your Property Is Risky Self-insuring means setting aside your own money to cover potential losses, instead of paying for a traditional insurance policy. While it might seem cheaper upfront, this strategy comes with serious downsides. Florida’s coastal location makes it especially vulnerable to hurricanes, windstorms, and flooding. If your home suffers damage and you’re self-insured, you’ll be on the hook for the full cost of repairs - expenses that can easily soar into the tens or even hundreds of thousands of dollars. In short: self-insuring is not a realistic or safe option for most Florida homeowners. The Smarter Option: Dwelling Fire Coverage That’s where dwelling fire insurance comes in. Often referred to as “landlord insurance,” these policies are available to both rental and primary residences. They offer coverage for core perils such as: Windstorm Hail Fire Lightning Vandalism Dwelling fire insurance provides a financial safety net without the high cost of a traditional homeowners policy. It’s a practical, budget-friendly way to secure your property while avoiding the high stakes of going uninsured. body_text: BBVA has completed the final tranche of the extraordinary share buyback program announced in December 2025. Between 6 May and 3 August 2026, the Group repurchased shares worth €1.46 billion, bringing to a close the largest share buyback program in its history, with a total value of €3.96 billion. Communications Listen to audio Leer en español In total, during this final tranche, which has now been completed, BBVA repurchased 70.3 million shares, representing 1.26% of the bank’s share capital as of today. The repurchased shares will be cancelled and, consequently, BBVA’s share capital will be reduced. With the completion of this extraordinary program, worth €3.96 billion, BBVA has now completed six share buyback programs, three of them extraordinary (the current programs, another worth €3.16 billion between 2021 and 2022, and one worth €1 billion in 2023) and three as part of its ordinary shareholder remuneration (worth €422 million charged against 2022, €781 million charged against 2023, and €993 million charged against 2024). BBVA maintains a strong capital position (with a CET1 ratio of 12.90% at the end of June), enabling it to continue growing strongly while maintaining an attractive shareholder remuneration, both through its ordinary policy and through its commitment to distribute excess capital above its 12% CET1 target on a progressive basis¹. Following this milestone, on 5 August the group will begin executing the first tranche, worth €1 billion, of the new extraordinary €2 billion share buyback program announced on 30 July². ¹Subject to the relevant approvals and authorizations. ² The execution of the remaining amount of the new share buyback program (€1 billion), and its terms, will be announced once they have been approved by the governing bodies.
